title: Granz insisting on unsegregated audiences
summary: Young saw Granz refuse to play in Lexington and Norfolk unless seating was mixed, and says money talks.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, he's a guy that fought that thing, that scene. He didn't like that scene and he fought it. I know he took us once, I think it was Lexington, Kentucky. And he told them if they didn't mix up that thing he wasn't going to play. Now, this is true. He did. I saw him do this. He did it.
Yeah, and he did it in Norfolk, Virginia too. I saw him do it.

Well, he wouldn't have played if they hadn't done it and they knew he wouldn't. Well, the promoters must have been pretty heavy, you know, because you'd be surprised what money people can do in situations like this because

they control -- they control the politicians and people like that anyway, the money people like that. They give them X amount of dollars to help put them in office and they carry an awful lot of weight. These money men have changed a lot of things. Well, you'd be surprised that -- what that dollar has done. That dollar is -- you can't change a person's heart but you sure can change around those things going on out there.

No, you can't make the money or whatever, power -- (unintelligible)? It won't make a person's heart condition change. That's why there will always be problems. But you can really -- you can really change a lot of those stupid laws out there. You can (inaudible).
